items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the poem 'A Concrete Example', and answer.

"Every spring, Mrs Kapoor bought a new packet of seeds and scattered them over the hard patch behind her flat. Every summer, the patch stayed stubbornly grey. Her neighbours joked that she was trying to grow roses on a road. But she only smiled, watered the stones and waited."

Answer the following:
(i) What did Mrs Kapoor do every spring?
(ii) What did the neighbours joke about?  (a) That she hated plants  (b) That she had too many flowers  (c) That she was trying to grow roses on a road  (d) That her garden was a forest
(iii) Which word shows that the patch refused to change?  (a) hard  (b) new  (c) grey  (d) stubbornly
(iv) How is Mrs Kapoor like Mrs Jones in the poem?
items.answer: (i) She bought seeds and scattered them over the hard patch. (ii) (c) That she was trying to grow roses on a road (iii) (d) stubbornly (iv) Both keep trying to grow a garden in hard, stony ground, and both are seen with gentle humour.
items.markingKey: (i) She bought seeds and scattered them over the hard patch. (ii) (c) That she was trying to grow roses on a road (iii) (d) stubbornly (iv) Both keep trying to grow a garden in hard, stony ground, and both are seen with gentle humour. (1 mark each, 4 marks.)
